newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel mutual funds post positive May returns.
newsitem.headline: Israel mutual funds post positive May returns.

text.p: Most of Israel's mutual funds posted positive real returns in May, a report by Meitav Investments and Securities said on Sunday.
Meitav's mutual fund index rose 3.5 percent in May, mainly because of the sharp rise of the equities market and the positive trend in the bond market.
In the first five months of the year Meitav's mutual fund index rose by 15.5 percent, with nearly all of the funds obtaining real positive returns.
Meitav said that in May the equities market strengthened its upward trend, with shares breaking new nominal records at the end of the month amid a steep rise in volume of trading.
"The frozen political, economic and interest rate situation did not manage to dampen the basic positive atmosphere of the equity market," the report said.
Meitav attributed the optimism to fairly low share prices and increased activity by foreign investors.

A lower-than-expected April consumer price index (CPI) and an expectation of low indices in the coming months caused prices of unlinked bonds to rise in May. But the central bank's decision to leave unchanged its key lending rate for June dampened the price rises, Meitav said.
Prices of unlinked bonds rose by 0.1 percent to 1.4 percent and prices of CPI-linked bonds rose by 0.5 percent only.
The strengthening of the shekel against the dollar caused prices of dollar-linked bonds to fall by 0.2 percent in May.
